title: Chinese Exclusion Act
summary: The US Congress passed, and President Chester A. Arthur signed, the Chinese Exclusion Act, approved on 6 May 1882. It banned Chinese laborers from immigrating for ten years and required certificates from other Chinese travelers. Sources describe it as the first law to place broad restrictions on US immigration.

uncertainty.note: Approval date 6 May 1882 per National Archives.

where.historical_name: Washington, District of Columbia, United States (seat of Congress; proxy pin for a nationwide law)

importance.justification: First broad federal restriction on US immigration, extended in 1892 and made permanent in 1902.

audience_note: Concerns a law that discriminated against people by ethnicity and nationality.
